EMERALD CHAMPIONS — GAME GUIDE, V4
================================

This book explains the game we are making. It owns the intended experience, story and design choices. Its short guide is followed by a generated reference containing exact teams, world data and source dialogue. Source files own those records; the reference is rebuilt and checked automatically. Test logs and development diaries stay outside the book. When a design changes, update this guide only where the experience changes and update the corresponding source at the same time.

Current focus: finish the integrated AI/Mega/release work, then audit major battle groups first: Elite Four/Champion, whole Gyms, Magma/Aqua arcs and the remaining trainers. The Cut-enclosure block and the Rusturf-to-Dewford team designs are implemented; the seven Brawly Gym designs, seven first-arrival beach/Seashore House designs and the reviewed blocks through Flannery are implemented:131 first-access encounters, including optional summit/Lavaridge battles and the early Ashen Woods detour. The retained roster is341 encounters; Gina and Mia remain an explicit keep. The next task is the major-battle-first design audit, with each trainer discussed in chat; full battle benchmarks and exhaustive AI validation are separate later work and do not block the next design group. The later earned C15 playthrough is a separate, paused development run; its save and unfinished Dwayne experiment are described in docs/CONTINUE.md. Reviewed teams are not automatically difficulty-tested. Later chapters below describe the intended campaign; native play and scene acceptance are unfinished.

1. THE EXPERIENCE
-----------------

Emerald Champions is a difficult competitive doubles adventure built on the native Emerald/Inclement/Expansion foundation. Battles should be memorable puzzles with strong Pokémon, useful support partners, competent AI and several lines of play. The player should improve at competitive decisions rather than spend hours fixing stats, acquiring ordinary equipment or repeating a grind.

The most important question after building or reviewing EVERY team is: “Could this team be cooler?” Ask it again after your own redesign. Judge the partnership, Pokémon choices, regional identity, alternate lines and counterplay. A legal team, a rare species or six filled slots is not enough. Keep a good low-stat or baby theme and adjust individual levels when strength is the problem. Do not evolve everything, replace unusual support with generic attackers or weaken correct AI just to make a fight easier.

Use a broad, coherent roster across generations. Preserve signature habitats and early useful choices. All supported Mega types should have meaningful opportunities, but a name on a checklist is not an executed showcase. Do not add battles or wild slots to satisfy quotas. Pokémon gifts, natural habitats, legendary scenes and opponent teams have different jobs; one does not substitute for the others.

Every retained campaign trainer uses doubles or a deliberately authored multi battle. Ordinary trainer teams generally have at least four members; every Gym trainer and leader has six. The player chooses two starters from one selected region and the rival uses the unchosen third. Ordinary wild and legendary captures remain singles. The opening Birch rescue is a bespoke low-level double before normal preparation.

Mega allocation and endgame rule — user direction, September14

All supported strategic Mega forms must receive a meaningful trainer-battle role. Stones, cosmetic variants and actually executed Mega showcases are separate coverage measures. The current source audit finds all99 stones held in permitted trainer slots, but Mega Rayquaza is not currently permitted on Steven's team; female Mega Meowstic, original-color Mega Magearna and the Droopy/Stretchy Mega Tatsugiri variants lack explicit owners. Mega Zygarde is conditional on Quincy's Power Construct reaching Complete Form first. None of those gaps is declared battle-validated. Exact coverage: work/trainer-through-flannery-implementation/mega-coverage.json.

Ordinary trainers and the player retain one Mega Evolution per battle. Sidney, Phoebe, Glacia, Drake, Champion Wallace and the final optional former-Champion Steven exhibition may execute at most two. The budget belongs to the trainer, persists across switches and fainting, and counts actual transformations; it does not reset for a new battler. Existing slot permissions still apply. The engine support has focused native activation, budget, owner and execution-guard validation. The five League pairings are now approved and implemented as listed below; the separate Steven exhibition remains for its own review. No Gym leader gets the two-Mega exception by default. Flannery has Mega Chandelure; Gerald Mega Charizard X, Eli Mega Camerupt and Danielle Mega Blaziken provide the other Lavaridge showcases.

The next design audit starts with Elite Four/Champion, then whole Gyms and Magma/Aqua story groups, then remaining trainers. Allocate rare species, Megas and major strategies around those core battles before refining nearby lower-tier encounters. Existing first-access coverage remains evidence of reviewed designs and access, not the required ordering of future design discussions.

Approved Elite Four and Champion block — September14

All five encounters remain six-member doubles fights at incoming player cap96. Each boss can use two actual Mega Evolutions, announced before battle. Pairings: Sidney Sharpedo/Absol Z; Phoebe Banette/Gengar; Glacia Froslass/Baxcalibur; Drake Salamence/Dragonite; Wallace Milotic/Starmie. They are ten different Mega forms, and the five complete teams share no Pokemon species. Exact moves, items, investment and individual cap-relative levels are materialized from the trainer authoring source; this does not establish final battle difficulty. Native ownership/permission checks and pairing probes are recorded separately from full-fight calibration.

SIDNEY: Dark Aura pressure with protected fast finishers. Replace Darkrai with Light Clay Grimmsnarl and Hoopa-Unbound with Speed Boost Sharpedo. Keep Incineroar/Yveltal as the opening, Urshifu as the protection-breaking reserve and Mega Absol Z as the fast Magic Bounce threat. Yveltal gains Heat Wave over Snarl and Life Orb for special pressure. Stats: Incineroar and Grimmsnarl receive compensating level100 support seeds; Yveltal is fast special; Sharpedo/Absol/Urshifu fast physical. Mega Sharpedo gets Strong Jaw for Crunch/Psychic Fangs, not Liquidation. Dark Aura boosts eligible Dark attacks on both sides. Could it be cooler? Sharpedo can earn a Speed Boost before Mega Evolution, then trade its ability for Strong Jaw; the Mega decision is a timing choice. Psychic Fangs removes screens. Mega Absol Z uses its151 base Speed and Magic Bounce to punish direct status targeting; it does not grant teamwide reflection. Overrepresented? Sharpedo is also an Archie showcase; Sidney adds Dark Aura and a second Dark Mega rather than another rain room. Absol Z stays Sidney's exclusive named form. Darkrai/Hoopa are released for more deliberate homes rather than included only for their power. Medium cap96 levels 100/96/100/97/98/96 are initial design seeds; complete battle calibration remains pending. Counterplay: Fairy pressure, burns on eligible physical attackers, screen removal, Trick Room, priority and denying Sharpedo a safe setup/activation window. Dark types obstruct Grimmsnarl Prankster Thunder Wave. No Dark Void coin flip is required.

PHOEBE: Ghost trapping, Encore and boost punishment. Mega Banette replaces Dusclops. Mega Gengar keeps trapping/control; Banette supplies Poltergeist/Encore/Will-O-Wisp/Protect. Lunala replaces Calm Mind with Wide Guard and gets Timid/Cloak. Keep Giratina, Marshadow and Specs Spectrier. Stats: Physical Giratina supports and survives; Lunala and Spectrier attack specially; Marshadow/Banette exploit physical lanes. Banette uses its165 Mega Attack with HP investment and priority utility. Gengar receives95 as a starting seed for170 Special Attack/130 Speed; this is not proven balanced. Could it be cooler? Gengar can trap a foe while Banette Encores an already-used move. Lunala's Wide Guard covers applicable spread attacks; Marshadow steals opposing boosts. This is a coordinated trap/control team, without inventing Perish Song. Overrepresented? Gengar and Banette exist earlier as individual Megas; Phoebe combines them and has no species overlap with the other four League teams. Keep its ghost identity rather than add another weather setter. Medium cap96 levels 97/96/96/100/97/95 are initial design seeds; complete battle calibration remains pending. Counterplay: Ghost types can escape Shadow Tag, valid pivots can escape, Dark types block hostile Prankster, and Taunt/ability suppression/priority or special mitigation can disrupt the formation. Poltergeist requires the target to hold an item. Spectrier's Grim Neigh needs a knockout, not just a teammate's KO.

GLACIA: Snow endurance with physical and special closers. Mega Froslass replaces Articuno as the fast special reserve and second Snow Warning opportunity. Ninetales keeps Aurora Veil; Froslass uses Blizzard/Shadow Ball/Icy Wind/Protect. Keep Specs Kyurem, Chien-Pao, Slush Rush Sandslash and Mega Baxcalibur; Baxcalibur gains High Horsepower over redundant Ice Shard. Stats: Ninetales invests in HP/Speed; Kyurem special offense; Chien-Pao/Sandslash/Baxcalibur physical offense; Froslass fast special. Mega Baxcalibur has175 Attack/115HP/117Defense and retains Thermal Exchange. Snow's Ice Defense bonus does not cover special attacks. Could it be cooler? If the first snow setter goes down or weather is replaced, Mega Froslass can establish the second snow phase through actual Mega activation. Sword of Ruin and the physical sweepers convert that window into pressure; Icy Wind offers speed control when snow-speed alone does not solve the board. Overrepresented? This is the League culmination of Lucas's snow formation. No unnecessary third snow setter or fourth generic Ice setup sweeper. Froslass/Baxcalibur are separate offensive roles and do not duplicate another League Mega. Medium cap96 levels 100/95/96/97/100/96 are initial design seeds; complete battle calibration remains pending. Counterplay: Weather replacement, strong special Fire/Fighting coverage, screen removal and denying the fast attackers. Sword of Ruin also reduces eligible teammates' Defense; snow is not an excuse to ignore that liability. Glaive Rush leaves its real retaliation risk.

DRAKE: Mixed Dragon air force with a sun phase. Salamence receives Salamencite and Double-Edge/Earthquake/Tailwind/Protect. Replace Mega Garchomp with specially offensive Mega Dragonite: Draco Meteor/Air Slash/Flamethrower/Roost. Keep Reshiram/Zekrom/Koraidon/Regidrago; Regidrago gains Earth Power over redundant Dragon Pulse. Stats: Mega Salamence uses145 Attack/120 Speed and Aerilate Double-Edge; Mega Dragonite uses145 Special Attack, broad bulk and Multiscale. Their physical/special roles differ. Koraidon and the high-BST dragons use restrained individual seeds rather than raising every member equally. Could it be cooler? The airborne Mega pair creates a safe Earthquake partnership; the other four allies are grounded, so Earthquake is conditional and often wrong beside them. Koraidon supplies actual sun for Reshiram and Dragonite Flamethrower. Air Slash avoids Hurricane's sun accuracy penalty. Overrepresented? Mega Garchomp is freed for an actual sand home, preserving the distinctive ordinary Mega rather than distorting Drake around an inactive Sand Force. Mega Rayquaza remains a separate allocation question for the final Steven exhibition; it is not piled onto this team as a third Mega. Medium cap96 levels 96/96/97/95/98/98 are initial design seeds; complete battle calibration remains pending. Counterplay: Fairy immunity, Ice pressure, Wide Guard against Dragon Energy/Earthquake, weather or speed control, and chip breaking Dragonite Multiscale. Draco Meteor lowers Special Attack and Roost changes Dragonite's temporary grounding/type interaction; neither is a free loop.

WALLACE: Rain and mist with a durable special anchor and physical Mega finisher. Make Wallace's signature Milotic the second Mega with Miloticite and Muddy Water/Helping Hand/Recover/Ice Beam. Keep Huge Power physical Mega Starmie, Kyogre/Tapu Fini leads, Ferrothorn and Palkia. Give Ferrothorn zero Speed IVs. Stats: Mega Milotic is Water/Fairy with95HP/109Defense/155Special Defense; Prism Scales reduces incoming special damage by30%, so HP/Defense investment covers its weaker side. Mega Starmie has100 Attack doubled by Huge Power and120 Speed. Kyogre/Palkia stay special, avoiding an all-physical ending. Could it be cooler? Kyogre starts rain while Fini starts Misty Terrain; each field is independently replaceable. Later Milotic can use priority Helping Hand for Starmie or recover when doing so buys progress. Milotic's base Competitive phase can punish a real stat drop before it Mega Evolves; the ability changes to Prism Scales afterward. Overrepresented? Milotic is Wallace's own signature, so this pairing strengthens his identity. Starmie's unusual physical Mega stays reserved for the Champion. Keep Ferrothorn's Grass/Steel resistance and Palkia's rain Thunder rather than replace every supporting species with another legendary. Medium cap96 levels 96/100/100/96/98/97 are initial design seeds; complete battle calibration remains pending. Counterplay: Change rain, change terrain, use Wide Guard, target the physical/special lane appropriately, pressure Kyogre before Water Spout, and punish a passive Recover turn. Mist does not cure existing status; sun/rain changes do not remove it. Palkia intentionally avoids Dragon STAB into grounded targets protected by mist.

Distribution decisions: Darkrai/Hoopa-Unbound leave Sidney; Dusclops leaves Phoebe; Articuno leaves Glacia; ordinary Mega Garchomp leaves Drake for a meaningful sand home elsewhere. These are opponent-role decisions, not changes to player availability or permission to remove a protected species. Mega Rayquaza remains for a later Steven allocation discussion. All existing stone acquisition sources remain unchanged. No extra League battles, roster cuts, automatic healing or player Mega allowance are added. Next review: whole Gyms as a group, then Magma/Aqua story groups. Continue tracking the unresolved form-coverage gaps before claiming every Mega is showcased.

2. RULES, PREPARATION AND PROGRESSION
-----------------------------------

The first Oldale visit, before the prepared Route103 rival, provides healing, storage, the Leveler, legal moves and build editing. Nature, ability, EVs, useful IVs, friendship and ordinary battle equipment are free preparation choices. Maximum PP is fixed at its fully improved value. A preset is a convenience, not a different legality system or permission to manufacture progression items. All ordinary battle berries are freely available for equipping and planting; they cannot become free manual medicine or resale profit.

Manual medicine and X-items cannot brute-force trainer or wild fights. Poké Balls remain usable for catches, and held effects and healing/revival moves remain ordinary battle mechanics. Battle-start held items, including consumed berries, are restored at settlement. Field Potions, Revives, status cures and PP recovery remain exploration conveniences. Centers, the refillable Vial and established rest points reduce the need to purchase them.

Easy, Medium and Hard adjust enemy levels only, by −4/−2/0 relative to the authored individual offsets (src/difficulty.c). Medium is the new-game default. They do not change teams, AI, story or the player cap. Each trainer member uses the live player cap plus its authored individual offset and the difficulty adjustment. Optional return fights scale with the live cap and award no prize money; old absolute levels in generated trainer records are previews. Opponents can exceed100 within the native1–255 representation. No hidden stat multiplier replaces level tuning.

Player caps rise after milestones, not during their boss fights. Captures, gifts, evolution and preparation respect the current individual cap. Legendary/mythical species above600 configured BST use floor(chapter cap ×600/BST), with a minimum of1. Species at or below600 retain the chapter cap. Ultra Beasts/Paradox species are not automatically restricted. Temporary Mega/Primal forms do not incur a second reduction. No additional Mega-ready penalty is approved.

Caps: opening14; Roxanne20; Dewford manor/song24; Wattson30; Mt. Chimney36; Flannery42; Norman48; weather survey54; Winona60; Faraway return68; Heatran76; Space Center84; Juan90; Victory Road Wally96; Champion100. The entire League is fought at96.

Evolution must work locally, without another emulator or online trade. Linking Cord is reusable; item evolutions use the corresponding item locally while retaining meaningful form, gender, location and party conditions. Free bonding and move preparation support friendship and known-move evolutions. The Leveler permits evolution confirmation at the cap; decline and Everstone remain valid. Repetitive walking, move-use, recoil and critical-hit chores have been removed for their explicitly amended species; do not replace them with a new currency, ticket or invented level floor. Finizen evolves at38 and Gimmighoul at45 in the current rules. Exact relationships are in the configured species tables.

Key items register to SELECT, L or R from the Bag's Register action, one item per button; the Bag list shows the bound button beside the item. The L slot is inactive while the L=A button option is on. R without a bound item keeps its DexNav search. Registered bindings survive Save and Continue.

Field access requires the relevant badge and license. Cut: Rustboro cutter, usable after Roxanne. Flash: Granite Cave hiker, usable with Stone Badge before Brawly; lower floors light on entry without consuming a moveslot. Rock Smash: Mauville provider, usable after Wattson. Strength: Rusturf reunion, usable after Flannery. Surf: Wally's family after Norman. Fly: Route119 rival, usable after Winona. Dive: Steven after Space Center. Waterfall: final Sootopolis handoff, usable after Juan. A compatible party member can perform an unlocked field move without occupying a moveslot. Research transport is separate from personal Fly.

3. THE CAMPAIGN
---------------

ONE STORY AND ONE REQUIRED ORDER
The required story spine is C01 → first-arrival C03 access → C02 → C04 → C05 → C07 → C08 → C09 → C10 → C12 → C13 → C14 → C16 → C17 → C18 Wally → C19 → C20 reunion → C22 → C23 → C24 → C25 → C26 → C27 → C28 → C29 → C30 → C31 rival/Scope/Winona → C32 rival/harbor → C34 first voyage → C35 → C36 → C37 → C38 → C39 → C40 → C41 → C42 → C46 → C47 → C48 → C49 → C50. C43 Birth Island, C44 the Scanner and C45 the Sealed Chamber and three ruins are optional once the Space Center grants Dive and island passage.

STORY GATE ENFORCEMENT — SEPTEMBER14 USER DIRECTION
Transitions enforce required accomplishments rather than relying on suggested dialogue: museum after Dewford; Wattson after museum/Wally; Flannery after Chimney; Norman after C26; Weather Institute after C28; Winona after C30 and Scope; new expedition permissions after survey/Scope/Winona and the Lilycove rival; Magma Maxie after C36; Heatran after Maxie's completed Groudon scene; submarine theft/Aqua finale after Heatran; twins after Aqua finale; Space Center after twins; Seafloor climax after Space Center; Birth Island, the Scanner report and the Sealed Chamber ruins are optional after the Space Center; Juan after crisis; Diancie/Jirachi after Badge8; League after Steven's C48 conclusion and eight badges. Earned return transport and healing remain available. Blocked interactions explain the prerequisite and destination. Kyogre's awakening still leads immediately through Sootopolis and Sky Pillar, with no intervening side quest.

C06, C11, C15, C21, C33 and optional services within other chapters are route/preparation opportunities, not requirements to spend, breed, harvest, collect or win optional fights. Required licenses and story interactions at those places remain explicitly named. Story scenes gate the next required event in this spine. Ordinary healing, return transport, preparation and access to already-open habitats remain available. Kartana's preserved access is not changed by this ordering.
Research is what characters sometimes do within this story; it is not a second progression track. Internal report/accomplishment identities may record persistence, but the player receives concrete dialogue and consequences. Generic report turn-ins do not become extra stages. Capturing a named legendary is optional unless an explicitly optional acquisition itself requires it.

C01 — A journey with two partners
Choose both starters and rescue Birch in the existing opening. Birch sees that you can coordinate a pair and encourages the journey. Preserve the rival's remaining-third-starter rule. Initial cap: 14.

Retained exact contract:
Starter identity contract: record generation, first selected starter and second selected starter independently. The rival uses the remaining third regional starter, as 7.1 GetEmeraldChampionsRivalStarterIndex does; character gender selects the presentation variant. Old TRAINER ID suffixes are not a reason to give the rival one of the player’s selected partners. Both starter ownership records stay separate.

PLAYER HANDOFF — Birch at the rescue/send-off interaction:
“Go north from Littleroot along Route 101 to Oldale. Heal and prepare at its Pokémon Center, then take the north exit to Route 103 and meet your rival.”
Repeat availability: the same existing interaction keeps the current direction until its destination event is completed; when it cannot remain, use the existing departure interaction as described in the navigation contract.

C03 — Oldale before the first real test
On the first visit, the Center gives practical access to preparation, healing, storage, the Leveler and catching supplies. Let the player try those services before continuing north. This stop supplies the tools for the game without making every tutorial mandatory.

Retained exact contract:
ACCESS CLARIFICATION: these services are available on FIRST arrival in Oldale, before E0001 on Route103. The chapter numbering is not a service lock. Free preparation/healing, basic Balls, normal catching and storage must work before that prepared rival; Pokédex/send-off completion afterward is not a prerequisite. C02 therefore includes the optional Oldale preparation stop before its rival sub-event.

Oldale's west-exit blocker gives the same current direction when spoken to or approached through the blocked path: prepare at the Center and meet the rival through the north exit before that battle; afterward, follow Route101 south to Birch's Littleroot lab for the send-off. The Leveler explanation identifies both badges and major discoveries as cap milestones.

C02 — Rival and send-off
Fight the rival on Route103, then return to Birch for the Pokédex and send-off. Birch's ten Great Balls use Bag then item-PC delivery; if neither fits, a Center nurse holds the gift while the send-off and Route102 access still complete. The rival's interest in your unusual two-partner journey establishes the recurring competitive relationship. Your immediate aim is Norman's Gym in Petalburg. As you leave town, Mom gives the Running Shoes and the Old Rod together and names the Route102 and Route103 ponds; a full Bag leaves the rod with her at home for the next visit, and Dewford's fisherman never issues a second rod. The Pokédex retains its native information pages. Forms are selectable across a paged grid, including the complete Alcremie family; moving beyond a page shows the next forms, B leaves selection, and START returns to Evolutions. Form selection and exits release their icons before opening the next screen. Evolution selection also retains every displayed target at the ten-row boundary, including Eevee's stone and location alternatives; cursor offsets never overwrite species records.

PLAYER HANDOFF — Rival after battle; Birch after the return:
“After the battle: return south through Oldale to Professor Birch's lab in Littleroot. After the lab send-off: go back to Oldale, take the west exit onto Route 102, and continue to Petalburg Gym to meet Norman.”
Repeat availability: the same existing interaction keeps the current direction until its destination event is completed; when it cannot remain, use the existing departure interaction as described in the navigation contract.

C05 — The ambush in Petalburg Woods
Rescue the Devon employee from the grunt. His survey records accompany Devon’s survey equipment, which is bound for Slateport; he does not yet know why the teams want their work. The attempted theft gives the player a personal reason to help when the equipment is stolen in Rustboro after Roxanne. Keep the existing woods scene, Rustboro theft scene and local habitats. Woods left/right approaches share the same reward branch; on full Bag the researcher names any Center nurse as the reclaim source, then exits normally. The later Rustboro one-ball reward uses a distinct receipt and likewise cannot hold up the Devon escort.

C06 — Rustboro
Meet the local specialists and obtain the existing Cut license. Evolution purchases and the Fidough trade remain optional choices. Devon's problem is unresolved, but the city's Gym challenge is the player's immediate step toward being able to travel farther.
The Center explains that IVs default to31 and remain freely adjustable through the tutor's Edit Stats service.

C07 — Roxanne
Defeat Roxanne. Her interest in stones provides a natural early connection to Steven without turning the Gym into a research exam. Steven gives Aerodactylite with the Mega Ring after Brawly. Roxanne gives no Mega Stone and never requires a return claim; her fossil receipt remains independent.

C09 — Devon and the two deliveries
Mr. Stone explains that the attempted theft concerns both Steven's work and Stern's marine surveys. The letter and equipment deliveries are one sensible journey through Dewford to Slateport. Devon funds the travel. Fossil revival remains an optional return service, not another report requirement.
If both the Key Items pocket and item PC are full, Mr. Stone holds the letter and the automatic introduction ends. Speaking to him retries delivery without replaying the escort; successful delivery then completes the PokéNav, travel funding and Briney handoff once.

C13 — Brawly and Mega access
Defeat Brawly, then return to Steven in his Granite Cave room to complete the letter/badge/Ring handoff. Brawly explicitly repeats those directions after the battle. Brawly's coordination test and the Ring expand the player's practical options. Steven supplies Aerodactylite with the Ring; every other stone, including starter-family stones, comes from its single established world source. Preserve the original overlapping Lilith/Brenden approach as ordinary back-to-back trainer encounters. Brenden may challenge immediately after Lilith, creating first-pass endurance pressure, but each victory persists independently. Losing to Brenden leaves Lilith defeated; the player can heal, rearrange the team and return to Brenden alone. Do not impose a full reset merely because sight lines overlap. Separately announced, deliberately balanced endurance challenges may require a restart from their first fight.

Retained exact contract:

C13 MEGA STONE ACCESS
Each of the99 item-based Mega Stones has exactly one authored acquisition source. Keep established world locations and remove overlapping trainer, story and starter gifts. Starter choices never create an additional stone entitlement. Charizardite X and Charizardite Y are different stones with their own individual locations. A full-storage retry belongs to the same original reward and keeps its original receipt. PC RELEASE refuses a Pokémon holding a protected item, including a Mega Stone, and asks the player to remove it first; releasing the holder must never delete the finite stone. The existing PC field-move safeguards also count non-Egg species compatible with an unlocked license, across party and boxes; an empty battle-move slot is neither loss nor proof of that capability.

PLAYER HANDOFF — Steven in Granite Cave after the Ring handoff:
“Go west from Dewford into Dewford Meadow and enter the manor. Read the historian's account, then speak to the meadow warden with any Pokémon that knows Sing. The Jigglypuff inside the manor already know it.”

4. BATTLES, ACCESS AND RECOVERY
------------------------------

The current finite roster contains341 encounters across324 authoring groups and368 party variants. Gender/starter aliases and two-owner definitions are not extra played battles. Stable trainer IDs are not chronological numbering. Exact rosters and plans are authored in data/emerald_champions/emerald_champions_battle_teams.txt; the compiler projects them into native parties and AI configuration.

Battle-removal policy and adopted ledger (reconciled September14)

The approved pacing direction is approximately30% fewer trainer encounters, selected from repetitive lower-tier ordinary/casual fights. Preserve Gym personnel, important rivals, bosses, League fights and meaningful expedition battles except the specifically adopted redundant story legs below. This is the existing curation program, not a request to remove another30% from the retained341. The roster remains open to further justified changes; compare actual pacing and distinct battle value rather than treating a count as a quality guarantee.

The historical first pass removed140 groups/142 trainer identities. E0014 Gina and Mia was deliberately restored by the user as the northern Route104 doubles encounter. They must remain an active battle; their restoration is an explicit keep decision, not an accidental reversal of a cut. The earlier ledger retains139 first-pass cut groups/141 identities, plus five additional v4 identities, totaling146 earlier retirements. The subsequent Angelina/Eric cuts below bring the current total to148. All146 are absent from active authored teams, nonempty native parties and Hoenn battle opcodes. Empty trainer metadata/IDs may remain for existing references; those are not playable battles. Civilian dialogue/actors are retained where authored. Earned traversal, civilian interaction and an exact unavoidable-playthrough reduction percentage remain unverified. The source-based receipt is work/trainer-85-100-implementation/cut-reconciliation.json.

Each battle needs a strong plan, a worthwhile fallback and sensible partner preservation. Shared AI reads the current board and already-committed player choices, never future RNG or uncommitted input. Its complete decision budget is1.2 seconds. Protect must buy real survival, recovery, positioning or partner payoff; neither a Protect quota nor stripping it wholesale solves poor decisions. Fix demonstrated shared defects across move and switch paths and verify the relevant exceptions.

A first-attempt win with fewer than three new faints prompts a difficulty review, not an automatic increase. Three failed optimized attempts prompt a review of preparation, mistakes and individual levels, not endless retries. Use strong stage-legal alternatives, including legitimately accessible legends. Assisted party preparation is allowed for development with acquisition evidence; it does not count as native catching acceptance.

Retry restores the current battle checkpoint; Reload restores the last saved game. They remain separate. Ordinary adjacent fights retain individual clears and first-clear rewards. Museum and summit/Space Center legs release field control and allow recovery trips without replaying completed legs; no unannounced free heal is added. Lilith/Brenden retain this independent-clear rule. Steven's explicit team-up heal and full-party restoration are exceptions stated before selection.

Winstrates are an announced optional four-fight endurance challenge: no between-leg healing/editing, with continue/withdraw choices. Failure or withdrawal restarts the attempt at Victor, but permanent payouts cannot be farmed. The League allows field medicine/Vial and existing portable preparation between rooms, but no new Center, PC, shop or free refill. Bring six; abandoning or ordinary defeat resets the sequence at the outside recovery point. Retry restarts the current leg. Permanent first-clear payouts and Champion completion remain single entitlements.

5. REWARDS AND ECONOMY
---------------------

Agreed economy direction: ordinary play should fund several reasonable team rebuilds; substantial spending choices belong mainly to optional Pokémon and Megas. This section owns that design direction. Generated section C maps the current implementation by location and reward with code references. The September14 implementation below applies affordable evolution prices and dependable early Cord access. The later single-source Mega policy supersedes the earlier Lilycove purchase alternatives. Further reward redistribution needs location-specific design; the source atlas remains the complete current allocation. We are not adding collectible locations to fill a reward quota. Existing Emerald/Inclement pickups, NPCs, shops and event handoffs provide the delivery budget. Prefer replacing an unwanted item at a verified existing location over adding a sparkle, hidden item or actor. New playable choreography explicitly required by the story is separate work.

Reward value comes primarily from new Pokémon options: evolution items, appropriate Mega Stones, fossils, useful gifted Pokémon and meaningful encounter access. Capture supplies are useful secondary rewards. Money matters only while it buys wanted choices. Ordinary held items, stat editing and move preparation are already free and should not be sold back to the player as progression prizes. Field healing is useful convenience but a weak default reward for an interesting early detour.

Slateport decoration-shop membership guidance points to the Secret Power camper beside the large tree on Route111 north of the desert. His introduction unlocks the stock; no TM ownership or purchase is required. Creating a Secret Base also qualifies.

Evolution purchases cost500 per stone,1000 per ordinary tool and3000 per reusable device. Rustboro sells its six common stones plus Linking Cord from first arrival; Slateport adds the other stones and imported tools; Lilycove provides the complete paid catalogue. Linking Cord must be available through a dependable early purchasing route, with optional gifts saving a purchase. Item-use trade evolutions remain local. Fossil revival is free; acquiring the fossil is the reward. Free species-dependent form tools are not paid stat improvements. No new evolution ticket or specialist currency is proposed where the existing item/service works.

Player Mega Stones start with the bracelet. Align each stone with obtainable matching family and a practical evolution path; map presence, old review order or an opposing Mega is insufficient. Roxanne's Old Amber → Devon Aerodactyl → Steven's bracelet/Aerodactylite is the first concrete pairing. Starter choices do not create an extra Mega Stone entitlement. Later stones can use existing exploration endpoints, meaningful existing NPC gifts or a few selected opponents rewarding the Mega they showcase. No automatic stone drop from every Mega trainer or free global archive. Each Mega Stone retains one world acquisition source. The former four-stone Lilycove purchase alternatives are removed; trainer holding/evolution eligibility is separate from the player acquisition route.

Mega/evolution access cross-check (September14): work/mega-evolution-access-20260914/source-audit.json links all99 stones to world sources and candidate matching-family providers, using actual form-change tables. All45 configured evolution-item requirements have Lilycove shop stock, and all30 trade branches have local item alternatives; Karrablast/Shelmet still require the counterpart in the party. Four regional evolutions are not local methods: Pikachu to Alolan Raichu, Exeggcute to Alolan Exeggutor, Cubone to Alolan Marowak and Mime Jr. to Galarian Mr. Mime still require absent Alola/Galar region values. Their intended direct wild captures remain available in Safari South/North/Northwest and the Shoal ice room, with existing NPC guidance. Source coverage is not sensible-timing acceptance: Dewford Barbaracite can arrive before Binacle can evolve at39. No all-stones stage/readiness or all-evolutions native reachability certification is claimed. The report records candidate providers and outstanding physical/story/usable-timing verification; it is evidence, not a second design authority.

Finite unique gifts need useful duplicate handling. The current design offers a one-time cash alternative for already-owned reusable devices or eligible duplicate Mega entitlements; shops refuse redundant reusable and Mega Stone purchases, scanning Bag, PC item storage, party, boxed and daycare held items; each purchase is limited to one. Cash compensation is only worthwhile if buying choices remain meaningful and must never become a repeatable free-stock loop. Already-claimed berry recipes do not charge or print money. Full Bag/PC preserves pending delivery and never requires winning the fight again.

Basic Balls are replenished freely up to10 at Centers. Specialized/bulk Balls are optional purchases. Current ordinary prices begin at100/300/600 for Poké/Great/Ultra Balls, with most specialist Balls600. Balls, free gear, keys and stones cannot produce resale loops. Starting money is6000; milestone stipends are implemented in src/caps.c and total44000 including starting cash and Champion. Trainer prizes and loot are additional. This is a funding schedule, not proof that every optional purchase is affordable when first encountered. Affordability itinerary:6000 starting cash buys the reusable3000 Cord plus six500 stone evolutions without any trainer income or stipend. Alternatively, six1000 tool evolutions cost6000 once their regional stock is reached. Existing first-clear trainer income and milestone stipends fund capture supplies and further rebuilds. Mega Stones are never sold; Poipole and Genesect are earned with Circuit BP, not cash. No stipend increase is needed for this basic preparation budget.

Harvested berries remain a distinct optional reward source. All67 ordinary berries are free equipment/planting seeds; only actual tree harvest yields per-type Harvest Pouch credit. Free gifts, presets, catches and restored held berries never mint credit. Planting uses an ordinary seed, not harvested credit. Ripe crops persist, growth is capped at four hours, and a full Bag or pouch leaves the crop intact. Recipe previews show have/need before payment. Existing plots are sufficient; no new mandatory garden or story harvest quota.

Current Berry Master recipes: Baxcalibrite for Razz6/Bluk6/Nanab4/Wepear4; Dragoninite for Cheri6/Chesto6/Oran6/Pecha6; Tyranitarite for Pomeg/Kelpsy/Qualot/Hondew/Grepa/Tamato4 each; Celebi invitation for Pinap8/Sitrus8/Lum4/Leppa8. The invitation unlocks an encounter, not a Pokémon gift. Failed attempts do not repay; Woods Celebi is an alternative sharing capture ownership. The reward choices and natural approach/yields must be evaluated in the new allocation plan.

Soot currently measures lifetime ash collection without spending:100 gives Linking Cord or its finite cash substitute,250 unlocks Marshadow discovery,500 gives Houndoominite or the finite duplicate alternative. Existing ash paths and Sack remain. Furniture costs ordinary money; a second soot purchasing balance and redundant flute economy are retired. None of these milestones gates the campaign or basic evolution. Reassess the late Cord reward as a money substitute, since players should already have a reliable Cord route.

Shoal Cave currently exchanges four Salt and four Shell for first Glalitite, then Big Pearl on later collections; already owning Glalitite closes the unique entitlement with a Pearl. Keep tide collection optional. We should decide whether the second tide visit earns enough value or should be shortened, rather than require waiting for a core progression item.

Colored shards currently buy corresponding evolution stones through Route124's treasure hunter. Coins buy an offered starter directly without gambling at500 coins (20 cash per coin); Poipole and Genesect are Circuit BP rewards instead. These are finite species entitlements. Circuit BP provides optional mastery rewards, not basic build editing. Paid shelves of free equipment, PP upgrades and X-items should stay retired. Currency conversion is not a substitute for a distinct desirable reward.

Bottle Cap/Hyper Training purchases have no meaningful role beside free IV editing and remain retired from the economy. The same applies to PP Up/Max, EXP grind rewards and paid duplicate move services. Residual engine items or disabled services are not automatically active player-facing economies. Audit actual providers before deleting code. Ordinary treasure can remain money; berries used for battle remain equipment; no currency deserves a system merely because Inclement had it.

Allocation order to agree: first identify the complete wanted pool and remove dead rewards; then reserve story licenses and unique character handoffs; then align Mega families/evolutions with actual access; then assign important exploration rewards to existing endpoints; finally fill ordinary paths with useful capture supplies, modest cash and occasional recovery. Use a small number of meaningful side activities. Each retained currency must answer what unique or cheaper wanted thing it buys, when it becomes useful, and why it deserves the player's time.

SHOP ROLES AND IMPLEMENTATION STATUS

Ordinary Marts provide dependable field supplies. Additional existing merchants carry understandable regional specialties, chiefly evolution access or specialized catching goods; ordinary customers can remain useful local voices without new shop menus. Buying nearby is a legitimate reason for overlapping stock.

Slateport retains its existing businesses: catching specialist; field-goods stall; herbal recovery/PP stall; dolls; decorations; and the Mart's imported evolution selection. Section C lists every current SKU, price rule, caller and stock condition. Do not move a stall or add a new seller merely to distribute more items.

Lilycove's roles are reception/lottery on1F, everyday supplies on2F, specialized catching and field recovery on3F, complete evolution stones/tools on4F, home/gifts on5F, and rooftop refreshments. The3F right clerk retains field recovery stock; Mega Stones have one world source each and no shop shelf. Existing cancellation, funds and capacity checks remain.

The Game Corner currently offers optional Coin purchases and Pokémon/doll prizes. Keeping Coins confined to a functioning optional arcade preserves its native identity; direct cash conversion was an earlier alternative, not an applied change. No required evolution, story key or mandatory clue may depend on gambling. Field medicine remains a useful local convenience, not a reason to occupy every specialist counter.

COMPLETENESS CONTRACT FOR THE ECONOMY ATLAS

Every source-backed entry identifies its location/actor or global rule, reward or stock, quantity/range, cost expression, condition/receipt statements and source reference. The reverse index finds other sources of the same reward. Native variable menus, random rewards, storage transfers and temporary/restored items are identified separately. A raw source mention or possible call path is not a promise that the player can collect it at that stage.

The generator checks all recognized acquisition/shop operations, configured prices, fixed trades, berry plots and held-item sources. New unclassified economic commands and unresolved graph paths appear in its coverage register. Completing the source map is not proof of every native transaction, geometry condition or affordability choice. Those are explicit acceptance work; no "mistake-proof" claim overrides evidence.

Integrated world-reward rules

MEGA REWARDS AND FAMILY ACCESS — APPROVED ECONOMY CLEANUP,2026-09-14
Keep Mega Stone discovery broadly coupled to obtainable Pokemon and their legal evolution access. Check actual route, rod, Cut/Surf/bike/story gates, evolution supplies and fossil revival; an encounter-table row or trainer holding a species does not prove player access. A stone should normally be usable now or on a clearly explained near-term evolution path, while special locations still feel special. No blanket transfer to a shop or free catalogue.
In a few selected later encounters, an opponent may give the Mega Stone its own team showcases after victory. Treat this as one authored finite reward with regional/character fit and an obtainable matching family, not an automatic reward from every Mega trainer. Tie the receipt to successful delivery independently of the battle clear; no mandatory repeat fight or invented new actor. Check other sources to avoid accidental redundant prizes. Future trainer reviews choose the actual recipients and update their exact scene/reward rows together.
Aerodactyl is the first concrete pairing: Roxanne first showcases Mega Aerodactyl in battle and explains the transformation afterward. The player's Mega Ring is still unavailable here. HARVESTED BERRIES: PER-TYPE OPTIONAL EXPLORATION REWARDS
All 67 supported ordinary berries are freely stocked at every Center held-item vendor from the beginning, in any team quantity the bag holds. Include status, recovery, resist, pinch/stat, flavor and special-effect berries. They remain equipment and planting seeds, not manual field medicine or sellable stock. No preset-stripping workaround is required.
Harvested berries are separate saved quantities for each berry type, displayed in the Harvest Pouch (Key Items). The vendor supplies the pouch for free and offers the same menu even if Key Items is full. Pouch/Center menus show all types, including zero, and all reward requests from the beginning. Each successful harvest grants its ordinary berry yield plus an equal number of harvested credits of that exact type. Only the shared tree-picking transaction mints these credits. Gifts, catalogue withdrawals, held-item swaps, battle restoration, catches, Blender/Crush and planting itself do not. Planting uses one ordinary seed; it never spends harvested credits.
Each type holds 255. A full berry bag or insufficient harvest-pouch capacity leaves the entire crop intact and awards nothing. Existing save offsets stay unchanged: the unused 88-byte Pokédex area contains the per-type byte counts and one encounter receipt. This is not an origin flag on interchangeable bag/held items; no retroactive credit for unidentified old bag stock.
Preserve existing garden locations and species identities. Growth takes at most four real-time hours per complete cycle for every type; original yield and watering bonuses remain. Ripe crops remain until picked. No main-story progression waits for gardening. Requests are visible early, collection across routes supplies much of them, and planting missing types is the optional shortcut. Prices are starting balance values; earned traversal must judge whether actual approach/yields require adjustment.

The Flower Shop explains free seeds, four-hour maximum ripening, watering/yield, persistent ripe fruit, exact-type harvest credits and early recipe previews at Center vendors. Its Wailmer Pail explanation must never claim fruit falls off; its ordinary gift supplies no harvest credit. Both first and repeated conversations share these updated texts. No menu-coordinate tutorial or compulsory gardening gate.

Finish the scene before giving control back. Every temporary party, camera state, map effect, movement lock and transport transition must settle on success, failure and cancellation. Milotic's base Competitive phase can punish a real stat drop before it Mega Evolves; the ability changes to Prism Scales afterward. Overrepresented? Milotic is Wallace's own signature, so this pairing strengthens his identity. Starmie's unusual physical Mega stays reserved for the Champion. Keep Ferrothorn's Grass/Steel resistance and Palkia's rain Thunder rather than replace every supporting species with another legendary. Medium cap96 levels 96/100/100/96/98/97 are initial design seeds; complete battle calibration remains pending.
  Counterplay: Change rain, change terrain, use Wide Guard, target the physical/special lane appropriately, pressure Kyogre before Water Spout, and punish a passive Recover turn. B. REGIONAL STARTERS — NATIVE RESOLVER
The unchosen third regional starter replaces the corresponding Hoenn seed slot. Exact runtime rules below are copied from their owner rather than hand-reimplemented in this generator.
src/emerald_champions_opening.c (includes first-rescue setup and starter/rival overrides):
#include "global.h"
#include "battle.h"
#include "battle_util.h"
#include "emerald_champions_battle_sets.h"
#include "emerald_champions_opening.h"
#include "event_data.h"
#include "item.h"
#include "pokemon.h"
#include "starter_choose.h"
#include "string_util.h"
#include "constants/emerald_champions.h"
#include "constants/flags.h"
#include "constants/items.h"
#include "constants/vars.h"

static const struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet sRescueSets[] =
{
    {
        .moves = {MOVE_CRUNCH, MOVE_PLAY_ROUGH, MOVE_SUCKER_PUNCH, MOVE_HELPING_HAND},
        .item = ITEM_FOCUS_SASH,
        .nature = NATURE_JOLLY,
        .ability = ABILITY_RATTLED,
        .evs = {4, 252, 0, 0, 0, 252},
    },
    {
        .moves = {MOVE_BELLY_DRUM, MOVE_EXTREME_SPEED, MOVE_SEED_BOMB, MOVE_PROTECT},
        .item = ITEM_SITRUS_BERRY,
        .nature = NATURE_ADAMANT,
        .ability = ABILITY_GLUTTONY,
        .evs = {4, 252, 0, 0, 0, 252},
    },
};

static void GetOpeningStarterSet(enum Species species, struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet *preset)
{
    const struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet *base = GetEmeraldChampionsRawBattleSet(species, 0);
    *preset = base != NULL ? *base : (struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet){0};
    if (species == SPECIES_CHIKORITA)
        preset->moves[0] = MOVE_GIGA_DRAIN;
    else if (species == SPECIES_TORCHIC)
    {
        static const struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet sTorchic =
        {
            .moves = {MOVE_FLAMETHROWER, MOVE_HELPING_HAND, MOVE_WILL_O_WISP, MOVE_PROTECT},
            .item = ITEM_EVIOLITE,
            .nature = NATURE_TIMID,
            .ability = ABILITY_SPEED_BOOST,
            .evs = {4, 0, 0, 252, 0, 252},
        };
        *preset = sTorchic;
    }
}

static bool32 CreateOpeningStarter(struct Pokemon *mon, u16 choice)
{
    enum Species species = GetStarterPokemon(choice);
    struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet preset;

    GetOpeningStarterSet(species, &preset);
    CreateRandomMonWithIVs(mon, species, 5, MAX_PER_STAT_IVS);
    return ApplyEmeraldChampionsScriptedSet(mon, &preset) == EC_BATTLE_SET_SUCCESS;
}

bool32 GiveEmeraldChampionsStarterPair(u16 first, u16 second)
{
    struct Pokemon pair[2];

    // Commit both choices together before starting the rescue.
    if (first >= 3 || second >= 3 || first == second || CalculatePlayerPartyCount() != 0)
        return FALSE;
    if (!CreateOpeningStarter(&pair[0], first) || !CreateOpeningStarter(&pair[1], second))
        return FALSE;

    GiveScriptedMonToPlayer(&pair[0], 0);
    GiveScriptedMonToPlayer(&pair[1], 1);
    RecordPlayerPartyMonHeldItemForRestoration(0);
    RecordPlayerPartyMonHeldItemForRestoration(1);
    VarSet(VAR_STARTER_MON, first);
    VarSet(VAR_EC_SECOND_STARTER, second + 1);
    VarSet(VAR_EC_OPENING_STATE, EC_OPENING_PAIR_GRANTED);
    FlagSet(FLAG_SYS_POKEMON_GET);
    return TRUE;
}

u16 GetEmeraldChampionsSecondStarterIndex(void)
{
    return VarGet(VAR_EC_SECOND_STARTER) - 1;
}

bool32 HasEmeraldChampionsSecondStarter(void)
{
    u16 state = VarGet(VAR_EC_OPENING_STATE);

    return state >= EC_OPENING_PAIR_GRANTED && state <= EC_OPENING_COMPLETE
        && VarGet(VAR_EC_SECOND_STARTER) >= 1 && VarGet(VAR_EC_SECOND_STARTER) <= 3;
}

u16 GetEmeraldChampionsRivalStarterIndex(void)
{
    u16 first = VarGet(VAR_STARTER_MON);
    u16 second = GetEmeraldChampionsSecondStarterIndex();

    return 3 - first - second;
}

void BufferEmeraldChampionsRivalBranch(void)
{
    gSpecialVar_Result = (GetEmeraldChampionsRivalStarterIndex() + 2) % 3;
}

bool32 IsEmeraldChampionsBirchRescueBattle(void)
{
    return !IS_FRLG && (gBattleTypeFlags & BATTLE_TYPE_FIRST_BATTLE)
        && VarGet(VAR_EC_OPENING_STATE) == EC_OPENING_PAIR_GRANTED;
}

void CreateEmeraldChampionsBirchRescueParty(void)
{
    static const enum Species sSpecies[] = {SPECIES_POOCHYENA, SPECIES_ZIGZAGOON};

    ZeroEnemyPartyMons();
    for (u32 i = 0; i < ARRAY_COUNT(sSpecies); i++)
    {
        CreateRandomMonWithIVs(&gParties[B_TRAINER_OPPONENT_A][i], sSpecies[i], 2, MAX_PER_STAT_IVS);
        ApplyEmeraldChampionsScriptedSet(&gParties[B_TRAINER_OPPONENT_A][i], &sRescueSets[i]);
    }
    gPartiesCount[B_TRAINER_OPPONENT_A] = ARRAY_COUNT(sSpecies);
}

void ApplyEmeraldChampionsRegionalRivalSet(struct Pokemon *party, u32 slot, bool32 opening)
{
    enum Species species = GetMonData(&party[slot], MON_DATA_SPECIES);
    const struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet *base = GetEmeraldChampionsRawBattleSet(species, 0);
    struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet preset = base != NULL ? *base : (struct EmeraldChampionsBattleSet){0};

    if (opening)
    {
        GetOpeningStarterSet(species, &preset);
        // These are the rival's generated alternatives, not changes to the
        // player's starter presets. The party has no automatic sun setter.
        switch (species)
        {
        case SPECIES_BULBASAUR:
            preset.ability = ABILITY_OVERGROW;
            preset.moves[0] = MOVE_PROTECT;
            break;
        case SPECIES_CHARMANDER:
            preset.ability = ABILITY_BLAZE;
            preset.moves[1] = MOVE_FLAMETHROWER;
            break;
        case SPECIES_ROWLET:
            preset.moves[3] = MOVE_PROTECT;
            break;
        case SPECIES_SOBBLE:
            // Native preparation does not grant Sobble Ice Beam. Mud Shot
            // replaces redundant Water Pulse with legal coverage and control.
            preset.moves[2] = MOVE_MUD_SHOT;
            break;
        default:
            break;
        }
        if (preset.item == ITEM_EVIOLITE)
            preset.item = ITEM_SITRUS_BERRY;
    }
    else
    {
        switch (species)
        {
        case SPECIES_IVYSAUR:
            preset.ability = ABILITY_OVERGROW;
            preset.moves[0] = MOVE_SLEEP_POWDER;
            preset.moves[1] = MOVE_GIGA_DRAIN;
            preset.moves[3] = MOVE_PROTECT;
            break;
        case SPECIES_CHARMELEON:
            preset.ability = ABILITY_BLAZE;
            preset.moves[1] = MOVE_DRAGON_PULSE;
            break;
        case SPECIES_BAYLEEF:
            preset.moves[0] = MOVE_GIGA_DRAIN;
            break;
        case SPECIES_MONFERNO:
            // Fire STAB remains usable beside the rival's Lightning Rod.
            preset.moves[3] = MOVE_FIRE_PUNCH;
            break;
        case SPECIES_PRINPLUP:
            preset.moves[0] = MOVE_HYDRO_PUMP;
            break;
        case SPECIES_DRIZZILE:
            // Drizzile does not inherit Inteleon's Ice coverage. Preserve
            // Sniper/Focus Energy and add legal Electric coverage and speed control.
            preset.moves[2] = MOVE_MUD_SHOT;
            break;
        default:
            break;
        }
        // Campaign battles have no Item Clause. Preserve the canonical item
        // even when a partner also needs it (especially Eviolite).
    }
    ApplyEmeraldChampionsScriptedSet(&party[slot], &preset);
}

void GiveEmeraldChampionsOpeningBalls(void)
{
    gSpecialVar_Result = 0;
    if (AddBagItem(ITEM_POKE_BALL, 20))
        gSpecialVar_Result = 1;
    else if (AddPCItem(ITEM_POKE_BALL, 20))
        gSpecialVar_Result = 2;
    if (gSpecialVar_Result != 0)
    {
        VarSet(VAR_EC_OPENING_STATE, EC_OPENING_PRE_RIVAL_READY);
        VarSet(VAR_BIRCH_LAB_STATE, 3);
    }
}

void RestockEmeraldChampionsBasicBalls(void)
{
    u32 count = CountTotalItemQuantityInBag(ITEM_POKE_BALL);

    gSpecialVar_Result = 0;
    for (u32 i = 0; i < PC_ITEMS_COUNT; i++)
        if (gSaveBlock1Ptr->pcItems[i].itemId == ITEM_POKE_BALL)
            count += gSaveBlock1Ptr->pcItems[i].quantity;
    if (count >= 10)
        return;
    if (AddBagItem(ITEM_POKE_BALL, 10 - count))
        gSpecialVar_Result = 1;
    else if (AddPCItem(ITEM_POKE_BALL, 10 - count))
        gSpecialVar_Result = 2;
}

void BufferEmeraldChampionsStarterNames(void)
{
    StringCopy(gStringVar1, GetSpeciesName(GetStarterPokemon(VarGet(VAR_STARTER_MON))));
    StringCopy(gStringVar2, GetSpeciesName(GetStarterPokemon(GetEmeraldChampionsSecondStarterIndex())));
}

void SelectEmeraldChampionsStarterForNaming(void)
{
    u16 choice = gSpecialVar_0x8004 == 0 ? VarGet(VAR_STARTER_MON) : GetEmeraldChampionsSecondStarterIndex();
    enum Species species = GetStarterPokemon(choice);

    gSpecialVar_Result = FALSE;
    for (u32 i = 0; i < PARTY_SIZE; i++)
    {
        if (GetMonData(&gParties[B_TRAINER_PLAYER][i], MON_DATA_SPECIES) == species)
        {
            gSpecialVar_0x8004 = i;
            StringCopy(gStringVar1, GetSpeciesName(species));
            gSpecialVar_Result = TRUE;
            return;
        }
    }
}

C. COMPLETE ECONOMY SOURCE ATLAS
Current implementation. Proposed shop/reward changes remain separate in the guide. No source location is added or moved by this atlas.
Read by location below, or use the reverse reward index. Generated R/N/T references are lookup keys, not new gameplay IDs.
LITERAL means the source states the item/quantity. POTENTIAL PATH means a map entry can call that block in the source graph; it does not prove that every condition is satisfied in one save.
Receipts, daily flags, stock selection, hidden-object rules and costs are retained at their actual source owners. Variables and alternate delivery attempts are not flattened into fabricated independent rewards.
First physical access remains a separate geometry/story audit. The atlas contains the conditions needed to do that audit, not an invented first-badge number.

C2. SCRIPT TRANSACTIONS, SHOPS AND VARIABLE OFFERS
All effects are printed once; location entries link to them. A zero base price is not permission to obtain an item: the actual shop/free-service entry must exist.
Cash shop prices use GetItemPrice; sale events may apply the live discount in src/shop.c:GetShopItemPrice. BP/Coins/barter values are separate explicit costs.

    else if (JOY_NEW(DPAD_RIGHT))
    {
        if (!(gActionSelectionCursor[battler] & 1))
        {
            PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
            ActionSelectionDestroyCursorAt(gActionSelectionCursor[battler]);
            gActionSelectionCursor[battler] ^= 1;
            ActionSelectionCreateCursorAt(gActionSelectionCursor[battler], 0);
        }
    }
    else if (JOY_NEW(DPAD_UP))
    {
        if (gActionSelectionCursor[battler] & 2)
        {
            PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
            ActionSelectionDestroyCursorAt(gActionSelectionCursor[battler]);
            gActionSelectionCursor[battler] ^= 2;
            ActionSelectionCreateCursorAt(gActionSelectionCursor[battler], 0);
        }
    }
    else if (JOY_NEW(DPAD_DOWN))
    {
        if (!(gActionSelectionCursor[battler] & 2))
        {
            PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
            ActionSelectionDestroyCursorAt(gActionSelectionCursor[battler]);
            gActionSelectionCursor[battler] ^= 2;
            ActionSelectionCreateCursorAt(gActionSelectionCursor[battler], 0);
        }
    }
    else if (JOY_NEW(B_BUTTON) || gPlayerDpadHoldFrames > 59)
    {
        if (IsDoubleBattle()
         && GetBattlerPosition(battler) == B_POSITION_PLAYER_RIGHT
         && !(gAbsentBattlerFlags & (1u << GetBattlerAtPosition(B_POSITION_PLAYER_LEFT)))
         && !(gBattleTypeFlags & BATTLE_TYPE_MULTI))
        {

            if (gBattleResources->bufferA[battler][1] == B_ACTION_USE_ITEM && GetItemConsumability(itemId))
            {
                AddBagItem(itemId, 1);
            }
            PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
            BtlController_EmitTwoReturnValues(battler, B_COMM_TO_ENGINE, B_ACTION_CANCEL_PARTNER, 0);
            BtlController_Complete(battler);
        }
        else if (B_QUICK_MOVE_CURSOR_TO_RUN)
        {
            if (!(gBattleTypeFlags & BATTLE_TYPE_TRAINER))
            {
                PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
                ActionSelectionDestroyCursorAt(gActionSelectionCursor[battler]);
                gActionSelectionCursor[battler] = 3;
                ActionSelectionCreateCursorAt(gActionSelectionCursor[battler], 0);
            }
        }
    }
    else if (JOY_NEW(START_BUTTON))
    {
        SwapHpBarsWithHpText();
    }
    else if (DEBUG_BATTLE_MENU == TRUE && JOY_NEW(SELECT_BUTTON))
    {
        BtlController_EmitTwoReturnValues(battler, B_COMM_TO_ENGINE, B_ACTION_DEBUG, 0);
        BtlController_Complete(battler);
    }
    else if (B_LAST_USED_BALL == TRUE && B_LAST_USED_BALL_CYCLE == FALSE
             && JOY_NEW(B_LAST_USED_BALL_BUTTON) && CanThrowLastUsedBall())
    {
        PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
        TryHideLastUsedBall();
        BtlController_EmitTwoReturnValues(battler, B_COMM_TO_ENGINE, B_ACTION_THROW_BALL, 0);
        BtlController_Complete(battler);
    }

    else if (ability == ABILITY_CHLOROPHYLL && holdEffect != HOLD_EFFECT_UTILITY_UMBRELLA && weather  & B_WEATHER_SUN)
        speed *= 2;
    else if (ability == ABILITY_SAND_RUSH   && weather & B_WEATHER_SANDSTORM)
        speed *= 2;
    else if (ability == ABILITY_SLUSH_RUSH  && weather & B_WEATHER_ICY_ANY)
        speed *= 2;


    if (ability == ABILITY_QUICK_FEET && gBattleMons[battler].status1 & STATUS1_ANY)
        speed = (speed * 150) / 100;
    else if (ability == ABILITY_SURGE_SURFER && gFieldTimers.terrain == B_TERRAIN_ELECTRIC)
        speed *= 2;
    else if (ability == ABILITY_SLOW_START && gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.slowStartTimer != 0)
        speed /= 2;
    else if ((ability == ABILITY_PROTOSYNTHESIS && !gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.transformed && weather & B_WEATHER_SUN) || gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.boosterEnergyActivated)
        speed = (GetParadoxBoostedStatId(battler) == STAT_SPEED) ? (speed * 150) / 100 : speed;
    else if (ability == ABILITY_QUARK_DRIVE && !(gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.transformed) && (gFieldTimers.terrain == B_TERRAIN_ELECTRIC || gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.boosterEnergyActivated))
        speed = (GetParadoxBoostedStatId(battler) == STAT_SPEED) ? (speed * 150) / 100 : speed;
    else if (ability == ABILITY_UNBURDEN && gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.unburdenActive)
        speed *= 2;


    if (!(gBattleTypeFlags & (BATTLE_TYPE_LINK | BATTLE_TYPE_RECORDED_LINK | BATTLE_TYPE_FRONTIER))
        && ShouldGetStatBadgeBoost(B_FLAG_BADGE_BOOST_SPEED, battler)
        && IsOnPlayerSide(battler))
    {
        speed = uq4_12_multiply_by_int_half_down(GetBadgeBoostModifier(), speed);
    }


    if (holdEffect == HOLD_EFFECT_MACHO_BRACE || holdEffect == HOLD_EFFECT_POWER_ITEM)
        speed /= 2;
    else if (holdEffect == HOLD_EFFECT_IRON_BALL)
        speed /= 2;
    else if (holdEffect == HOLD_EFFECT_CHOICE_SCARF && GetActiveGimmick(battler) != GIMMICK_DYNAMAX)
        speed = (speed * 150) / 100;
    else if (holdEffect == HOLD_EFFECT_QUICK_POWDER && gBattleMons[battler].species == SPECIES_DITTO && !(gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.transformed))
        speed *= 2;


    if (gSideStatuses[GetBattlerSide(battler)] & SIDE_STATUS_TAILWIND)
        speed *= 2;


    if (gBattleMons[battler].status1 & STATUS1_PARALYSIS && ability != ABILITY_QUICK_FEET)
        speed /= GetConfig(B_PARALYSIS_SPEED) >= GEN_7 ? 2 : 4;

    if (gSideStatuses[GetBattlerSide(battler)] & SIDE_STATUS_SWAMP)
        speed /= 4;

    return speed;

src/battle_main.c:GetDynamicMoveType | src/battle_main.c:5767
enum Type moveType = GetMoveType(move);
    enum BattleMoveEffects moveEffect = GetMoveEffect(move);
    enum Species species;
    enum Item heldItem;
    enum Type types[3];
    enum Gimmick gimmick = GIMMICK_NONE;

    if (state == MON_IN_BATTLE)
    {
        if (moveEffect == EFFECT_STRUGGLE)
            return TYPE_MYSTERY;

        species = gBattleMons[battler].species;
        heldItem = gBattleMons[battler].item;
        GetBattlerTypes(battler, FALSE, types);
        gimmick = GetActiveGimmick(battler);
    }
    else
    {
        species = GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_SPECIES);
        heldItem = GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_HELD_ITEM, 0);
        holdEffect = GetItemHoldEffect(heldItem);
        ability = GetMonAbility(mon);
        types[0] = GetSpeciesType(species, 0);
        types[1] = GetSpeciesType(species, 1);
        types[2] = TYPE_MYSTERY;
        gimmick = GIMMICK_NONE;
    }

    switch (moveEffect)
    {
    case EFFECT_WEATHER_BALL:
        if (state == MON_IN_BATTLE)
        {
            u32 weather =  GetAttackerWeather(holdEffect, ability, GetWeather());
            if (weather & B_WEATHER_SUN)
                return TYPE_FIRE;
            else if (weather & B_WEATHER_RAIN)
                return TYPE_WATER;
            else if (weather & B_WEATHER_SANDSTORM)
                return TYPE_ROCK;
            else if (weather & B_WEATHER_ICY_ANY)
                return TYPE_ICE;
            else
                return moveType;
        }
        else
        {
            if (ability == ABILITY_MEGA_SOL)
                return TYPE_FIRE;
            switch (gWeatherPtr->currWeather)
            {
            case WEATHER_DROUGHT:
                if (holdEffect != HOLD_EFFECT_UTILITY_UMBRELLA)
                    return TYPE_FIRE;
                break;
            case WEATHER_RAIN:
            case WEATHER_RAIN_THUNDERSTORM:
            case WEATHER_DOWNPOUR:
                if (holdEffect != HOLD_EFFECT_UTILITY_UMBRELLA)
                    return TYPE_WATER;
                break;
            case WEATHER_SNOW:
                return TYPE_ICE;
            case WEATHER_SANDSTORM:
                return TYPE_ROCK;
            }
            return moveType;
        }
        break;
    case EFFECT_HIDDEN_POWER:
        {
            u32 typeBits = 0;
            if (state == MON_IN_BATTLE)
            {
                typeBits = ((gBattleMons[battler].hpIV & 1) << 0)
                        | ((gBattleMons[battler].attackIV & 1) << 1)
                        | ((gBattleMons[battler].defenseIV & 1) << 2)
                        | ((gBattleMons[battler].speedIV & 1) << 3)
                        | ((gBattleMons[battler].spAttackIV & 1) << 4)
                        | ((gBattleMons[battler].spDefenseIV & 1) << 5);
            }
            else
            {
                typeBits = ((GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_HP_IV) & 1) << 0)
                        | ((GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_ATK_IV) & 1) << 1)
                        | ((GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_DEF_IV) & 1) << 2)
                        | ((GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_SPEED_IV) & 1) << 3)
                        | ((GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_SPATK_IV) & 1) << 4)
                        | ((GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_SPDEF_IV) & 1) << 5);
            }

            u32 hpTypes[NUMBER_OF_MON_TYPES] = {0};
            u32 i, hpTypeCount = 0;
            for (i = 0; i < NUMBER_OF_MON_TYPES; i++)
            {
                if (gTypesInfo[i].isHiddenPowerType)
                    hpTypes[hpTypeCount++] = i;
            }
            moveType = ((hpTypeCount - 1) * typeBits) / 63;
            return hpTypes[moveType];
        }
        break;
    case EFFECT_CHANGE_TYPE_ON_ITEM:
        if (holdEffect == GetMoveEffectArg_HoldEffect(move))
            return GetItemSecondaryId(heldItem);
        break;
    case EFFECT_REVELATION_DANCE:
        if (gimmick != GIMMICK_Z_MOVE)
        {
            if (state == MON_IN_BATTLE)
            {
                enum Type teraType;
                if (gimmick == GIMMICK_TERA && ((teraType = GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_TERA_TYPE)) != TYPE_STELLAR))
                    return teraType;
                if (types[0] != TYPE_MYSTERY && !(gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.roostActive && types[0] == TYPE_FLYING))
                    return types[0];
                if (types[1] != TYPE_MYSTERY && !(gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.roostActive && types[1] == TYPE_FLYING))
                    return types[1];
                if (gBattleMons[battler].volatiles.roostActive)
                    return (B_ROOST_PURE_FLYING >= GEN_5 ? TYPE_NORMAL : TYPE_MYSTERY);
                if (types[2] != TYPE_MYSTERY)
                    return types[2];

                return TYPE_MYSTERY;
            }
            else
            {
                return types[0];
            }
        }
        break;
    case EFFECT_RAGING_BULL:
        switch (species)
        {
        case SPECIES_TAUROS_PALDEA_COMBAT:
        case SPECIES_TAUROS_PALDEA_BLAZE:
        case SPECIES_TAUROS_PALDEA_AQUA:
            return GetSpeciesType(species, 1);
        default:
            break;
        }
        break;
    case EFFECT_IVY_CUDGEL:
        switch (species)
        {
        case SPECIES_OGERPON_WELLSPRING:
        case SPECIES_OGERPON_WELLSPRING_TERA:
        case SPECIES_OGERPON_HEARTHFLAME:
        case SPECIES_OGERPON_HEARTHFLAME_TERA:
        case SPECIES_OGERPON_CORNERSTONE:
        case SPECIES_OGERPON_CORNERSTONE_TERA:
            return GetSpeciesType(species, 1);
        default:
            break;
        }
        break;
    case EFFECT_NATURAL_GIFT:
        if (GetItemPocket(heldItem) == POCKET_BERRIES)
            return gBerries[ItemIdToBerryType(heldItem)].naturalGiftType;
        else
            return moveType;
    case EFFECT_TERRAIN_PULSE:
        if (state == MON_IN_BATTLE)
        {
            if (IsAnyTerrainAffected(battler, ability, holdEffect, gFieldTimers.terrain))
                return gBattleTerrainInfo[gFieldTimers.terrain].type;
        }
        else
        {
            switch (gWeatherPtr->currWeather)
            {
            case WEATHER_RAIN_THUNDERSTORM:
                if (B_THUNDERSTORM_TERRAIN)
                    return TYPE_ELECTRIC;
                break;
            case WEATHER_FOG_HORIZONTAL:
            case WEATHER_FOG_DIAGONAL:
                if (B_OVERWORLD_FOG >= GEN_8)
                    return TYPE_FAIRY;
                break;
            }
            return moveType;
        }
        break;
    case EFFECT_TERA_BLAST:
        if (gimmick == GIMMICK_TERA)
            return GetMonData(mon, MON_DATA_TERA_TYPE);
        break;
    case EFFECT_TERA_STARSTORM:
        if (species == SPECIES_TERAPAGOS_STELLAR)
            return TYPE_STELLAR;
        break;
    case EFFECT_NATURE_POWER:
        if (state == MON_IN_BATTLE)
            return GetMoveType(GetNaturePowerMove());
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }

    if (IsSoundMove(move) && ability == ABILITY_LIQUID_VOICE)
    {
        return TYPE_WATER;
    }
    else if (IsSoundMove(move) && ability == ABILITY_SAND_SONG)
    {
        return TYPE_GROUND;
    }
    else if (moveEffect == EFFECT_AURA_WHEEL
          && species == SPECIES_MORPEKO_HANGRY
          && ability != ABILITY_NORMALIZE)
    {
        return TYPE_DARK;
    }
    else if (moveType == TYPE_NORMAL
          && ability != ABILITY_NORMALIZE
          && gimmick != GIMMICK_DYNAMAX
          && gimmick != GIMMICK_Z_MOVE)
    {
        enum Type ateType = TrySetAteType(move, battler, ability);
        if (ateType != TYPE_NONE && state == MON_IN_BATTLE)
            gBattleStruct->battlerState[battler].ateBoost = TRUE;
        return ateType;
    }
    else if (moveEffect != EFFECT_CHANGE_TYPE_ON_ITEM
          && moveEffect != EFFECT_TERRAIN_PULSE
          && moveEffect != EFFECT_NATURAL_GIFT
          && moveEffect != EFFECT_HIDDEN_POWER
          && moveEffect != EFFECT_WEATHER_BALL
          && ability == ABILITY_NORMALIZE
          && gimmick != GIMMICK_Z_MOVE)
    {
        if (state == MON_IN_BATTLE && gimmick != GIMMICK_DYNAMAX)
            gBattleStruct->battlerState[battler].ateBoost = TRUE;
        return TYPE_NORMAL;
    }

    return TYPE_NONE;

    if (IsNPCFollowerWildBattle())

    switch (state)

        {


            gBattleCommunication[MULTISTRING_CHOOSER] = B_MSG_NO_MESSAGE_SKIP;
            gBattleCommunication[MULTIUSE_STATE] = GIVECAUGHTMON_GIVE_AND_SHOW_MSG;
            break;

#endif
        if (CalculatePlayerPartyCount() == PARTY_SIZE && B_CATCH_SWAP_INTO_PARTY >= GEN_7)
        {
            PrepareStringBattleWithWait(STRINGID_SENDCAUGHTMONPARTYORBOX, gBattlerAttacker);
            gBattleCommunication[MULTIUSE_STATE] = GIVECAUGHTMON_ASK_ADD_TO_PARTY;
        }
        else
        {
            gBattleCommunication[MULTISTRING_CHOOSER] = B_MSG_NO_MESSAGE_SKIP;

        gBattleCommunication[MULTIUSE_STATE] = GIVECAUGHTMON_HANDLE_INPUT;
        gBattleCommunication[CURSOR_POSITION] = 0;
        BattleCreateYesNoCursorAt(0);
        break;
    case GIVECAUGHTMON_HANDLE_INPUT:
        if (JOY_NEW(DPAD_UP) && gBattleCommunication[CURSOR_POSITION] != 0)
        {
            PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
            BattleDestroyYesNoCursorAt(gBattleCommunication[CURSOR_POSITION]);
            gBattleCommunication[CURSOR_POSITION] = 0;
            BattleCreateYesNoCursorAt(0);
        }
        if (JOY_NEW(DPAD_DOWN) && gBattleCommunication[CURSOR_POSITION] == 0)
        {
            PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
            BattleDestroyYesNoCursorAt(gBattleCommunication[CURSOR_POSITION]);
            gBattleCommunication[CURSOR_POSITION] = 1;
            BattleCreateYesNoCursorAt(1);
        }
        if (JOY_NEW(A_BUTTON))
        {
            PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
            if (gBattleCommunication[CURSOR_POSITION] == 0)
            {
                gBattleCommunication[MULTIUSE_STATE] = GIVECAUGHTMON_DO_CHOOSE_MON;
            }
            else
            {
                gBattleCommunication[MULTIUSE_STATE] = GIVECAUGHTMON_GIVE_AND_SHOW_MSG;
            }
            HandleBattleWindow(YESNOBOX_X_Y, WINDOW_CLEAR);
        }
        else if (JOY_NEW(B_BUTTON))
        {
            PlaySE(SE_SELECT);
            gBattleCommunication[MULTIUSE_STATE] = GIVECAUGHTMON_GIVE_AND_SHOW_MSG;
            HandleBattleWindow(YESNOBOX_X_Y, WINDOW_CLEAR);
        }
        break;
    case GIVECAUGHTMON_DO_CHOOSE_MON:
        if (!gPaletteFade.active)
        {
            BtlController_EmitChoosePokemon(gBattlerAttacker, B_COMM_TO_CONTROLLER, PARTY_ACTION_SEND_MON_TO_BOX, PARTY_SIZE, ABILITY_NONE, 0, gBattleStruct->battlerPartyOrders[gBattlerAttacker]);
            MarkBattlerForControllerExec(gBattlerAttacker);
            gBattleCommunication[MULTIUSE_STATE] = GIVECAUGHTMON_HANDLE_CHOSEN_MON;
        }
        break;
    case GIVECAUGHTMON_HANDLE_CHOSEN_MON:
        if (gSelectedMonPartyId != PARTY_SIZE)
        {
            if (gSelectedMonPartyId > PARTY_SIZE)
            {

                gSelectedMonPartyId = PARTY_SIZE;
                gBattleCommunication[MULTIUSE_STATE] = GIVECAUGHTMON_GIVE_AND_SHOW_MSG;
            }
            else
            {

                TryRevertPartyMonFormChange(gSelectedMonPartyId);



                if (GEN_LATEST == GEN_CHAMPIONS)
                    RestorePlayerPartyMonHeldItem(gSelectedMonPartyId);

                if (CopyMonToPC(&gParties[B_TRAINER_PLAYER][gSelectedMonPartyId]) == MON_GIVEN_TO_PC)
                {

        {

            lvlDivBy10 = (GetMonData(&gParties[B_TRAINER_PLAYER][i], MON_DATA_LEVEL)-1) / 10;
            if (lvlDivBy10 > 9)
                lvlDivBy10 = 9;

            ability = GetSpeciesAbility(species, GetMonData(&gParties[B_TRAINER_PLAYER][i], MON_DATA_ABILITY_NUM));

            if (ability == ABILITY_PICKUP
                && species != SPECIES_NONE
                && species != SPECIES_EGG
                && heldItem == ITEM_NONE
                && (Random() % 10) == 0)
            {
                if (isInPyramid)
                {
                    heldItem = GetBattlePyramidPickupItemId();
                    SetMonData(&gParties[B_TRAINER_PLAYER][i], MON_DATA_HELD_ITEM, &heldItem);
                }
                else
                {
                    u32 rand = Random() % 100;
                    u32 percentTotal = 0;

                    for (j = 0; j < ARRAY_COUNT(sPickupTable); j++)
                    {
                        percentTotal += sPickupTable[j].percentage[lvlDivBy10];
                        if (rand < percentTotal)
                        {
                            SetMonData(&gParties[B_TRAINER_PLAYER][i], MON_DATA_HELD_ITEM, &sPickupTable[j].itemId);
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            else if (ability == ABILITY_HONEY_GATHER
                && species != 0
                && species != SPECIES_EGG
                && heldItem == ITEM_NONE)
            {
                if ((lvlDivBy10 + 1 ) * 5 > Random() % 100)
                {
                    heldItem = ITEM_HONEY;
                    SetMonData(&gParties[B_TRAINER_PLAYER][i], MON_DATA_HELD_ITEM, &heldItem);
                }
            }
            else if (P_SHUCKLE_BERRY_JUICE == GEN_2
                && species == SPECIES_SHUCKLE
                && heldItem == ITEM_ORAN_BERRY
                && (Random() % 16) == 0)
            {
                heldItem = ITEM_BERRY_JUICE;
                SetMonData(&gParties[B_TRAINER_PLAYER][i], MON_DATA_HELD_ITEM, &heldItem);
            }
        }
    }

            break;

        tree->berryYield = 0;
        tree->stage = BERRY_STAGE_SPROUTED;
        tree->moistureLevel = 100;
        if (++tree->regrowthCount == ((tree->mulch == ITEM_TO_MULCH(ITEM_GOOEY_MULCH)) ? 15 : 10))
            *tree = gBlankBerryTree;
        break;
    }
    return TRUE;

src/berry.c:CalcBerryYieldInternal | src/berry.c:2666
u32 randMin;
    u32 randMax;
    u32 rand;
    u32 extraYield;

    if (water == 0 || OW_BERRY_MOISTURE)
    {
        return min;
    }
    else
    {
        randMin = (max - min) * (water - 1);
        randMax = (max - min) * (water);
        rand = randMin + Random() % (randMax - randMin + 1);


        if ((rand % NUM_WATER_STAGES) >= NUM_WATER_STAGES / 2)
            extraYield = rand / NUM_WATER_STAGES + 1;
        else
            extraYield = rand / NUM_WATER_STAGES;
        return extraYield + min;
    }

        || info->isGigantamax || info->isTeraForm)
        species = GET_BASE_SPECIES_ID(species);
    info = &gSpeciesInfo[species];
    if (!(info->isRestrictedLegendary || info->isSubLegendary || info->isMythical))
        return baseline;
    total = GetSpeciesBaseStatTotal(species);
    return total > 600 ? max(1, baseline * 600 / total) : baseline;

src/coins.c:AddCoins | src/coins.c:52
u16 newAmount;
    u16 ownedCoins = GetCoins();
    if (ownedCoins >= MAX_COINS)
        return FALSE;

    if (ownedCoins > ownedCoins + toAdd)
    {
        newAmount = MAX_COINS;
    }
    else
    {
        ownedCoins += toAdd;
        if (ownedCoins > MAX_COINS)
            ownedCoins = MAX_COINS;
        newAmount = ownedCoins;
    }
    SetCoins(newAmount);
    return TRUE;
